summary: Marianne Yaldiz is a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She served as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (attested 1997–2005) and the Museum für Indische Kunst (attested 2006).
Marie G. Wanek is a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy. She pursued her studies at the University of Pennsylvania under the instruction of Sengaku Mayeda.
Marie-Stella Boussemart studied under Dagpo Rinpoche and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Marina Illich is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University in 2006, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman, as well as Ryuichi Abe, Angela Zito, and John Stratton Hawley.

Mario D'Amato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1994–2000) under Paul J. Griffiths. He taught at Hampshire College (~2000–2001) and Rollins College (~2001–2006).

Mario Poceski earned his PhD from UCLA (2000) under Robert Buswell, specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He taught at the University of Iowa (2001) and became Assistant Professor at the University of Florida (attested 2004–2019).
Mario Praz studied at the Universities of Bologna (~1914–1918) and Florence (~1918–1920). He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and the University of Rome (~1934–1966).
Marion L. Matics is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Matics studied under doctoral supervisors Horace L. Friess and Royal W. Weiler, as well as under teacher Robert A. Fowkes.

Marion Meyer is an archaeologist and historian. She held posts at the German Archaeological Institute (1984–1985), the University of Florida (1996), the University of Bonn (~1997–2003), and the University of Vienna (~2003).

Marion Rastelli is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate under Gerhard Oberhammer. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2019) and the University of Vienna (attested 2020).

Mark A. Nathan completed his PhD in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology at UCLA in 2010 under Robert Buswell. In 2010, he held posts at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo.

Mark Allon, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD at Cambridge (~1989–1994) under Kenneth Roy Norman. He worked at SOAS (~1996–1999) and joined the University of Sydney around 2002.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2005) before becoming Professor of East Asian Languages and Cultures at the University of California, Berkeley (~2005).

Mark D. Griffiths earned a BSc from the University of Bradford and a PhD from the University of Exeter. He held a lectureship at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and became Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as professor of history at UC Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University (~2003).
Mark Hale works in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held positions at Harvard University (attested 1987) and Concordia University (attested 1997).

Mark I. Wallace earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1982–1986) under Paul Ricœur. Specializing in religious studies and philosophy, he taught at Georgia State University (~1987–1989) before becoming Professor of Religion at Swarthmore College (~1989).

Mark Jan Dresden studied at the Universities of Amsterdam and Utrecht, training under Jan Gonda, Harold Walter Bailey, and Walter Bruno Henning. A specialist in Iranian and Central Asian linguistics, he taught Iranian languages at the University of Pennsylvania (1949–1977).

Mark Juergensmeyer studied at the University of Illinois and earned a PhD from UC Berkeley (~1965–1974). A religious studies and Indology scholar, he became a professor at UC Santa Barbara (~1993) and Claremont McKenna College.
Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held an academic post as an associate professor at the State University of New York at Albany (attested 2004–2006).
